H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in Schenck v. United States (1919) did not hold that distributing leaflets urging resistance to the military draft is absolutely protected free speech during wartime. In fact, the Court held that the defendants' distribution of leaflets urging resistance to the draft was not protected speech because it presented a "clear and present danger" to the war effort (ID: 249_0047-01). The Court ruled that words which would normally be protected by the First Amendment can become subject to prohibition when they are used in circumstances that create a clear and present danger of bringing about substantive evils that Congress has a right to prevent.
